status: REGISTERED 2026-11-18: frozen BEFORE any registered dataset was generated or scored. Hashes of this file and of rmap_lib.py, rmap_run.py, rmap_report.py, rmap_jobs.txt, run_rmap.sh are in long_prereg_rmap.sha256. Any later change must be a dated addendum, not an edit.
approval: Proposed in chat on 2026-11-18 as Route 1 ('map when a quantum reservoir can win'). Student's words: 'let's run all'. The student confirmed the same day that novelty >= 7 is mandatory.
why: Novelty stayed 6 in six gate scorings because the copper result ('no quantum advantage') agrees with the literature. This test asks a different question: under which conditions of the data do the two published quantum reservoirs (DOM, ISING) beat matched classical models at all, and where does copper sit relative to those conditions.
not_copper: No copper data are read, generated or scored. All series are synthetic (rmap_lib.py). The copper placement step READS pooled ratios already written in dom4_report_rolling.csv. The stop rule of long_prereg_dom4.json (no further runs on the copper data) is therefore not affected.

design.process: x_{t+1} = b1 x_t + b2 mean(x_{t-9..t}) + b3 mean(x_{t-49..t}) + a g_t + e_{t+1}, e ~ N(0,1); 7000 steps after 500 burn-in.
design.structure_of_g: QDOM (Domingo G3 circuit, teacher seed 500+r, random Gaussian readout seed 600+r), QISING (Ising reservoir, seed 500+r), CESN (tanh echo state network, seed 500+r), CSAS (28-number state-affine system, the classical system with the same algebraic form as the quantum update), POLY2 (z_t z_{t-4}), POLY3 (z_t z_{t-1} z_{t-6}); centred and scaled to unit variance by constants from a pilot run with a = 0, clipped to +/-4. NULL = no g (share 0).
design.share: a = sqrt(s/(1-s)), s in {0.02, 0.05, 0.15, 0.30}; plus s = 0 (NULL). s is the intended share; because g feeds back into x the realised share differs, so the oracle ratio (true conditional mean vs HAR) is reported per cell.
design.cells_and_reps: 2 memories x (6 structures x 4 shares + NULL) = 50 cells; 10 independent datasets per cell (reps 0-9, separate noise and teacher seeds) = 500 datasets.
design.students_never_see_the_teacher: Student quantum reservoirs use circuit seeds 0-9; teachers use 500-509. Students use the copper pipeline's own scaling (min-max on training rows) and readout.
design.splits: Rows t = 50..6998 predict x[t+1]; train t < 4000; validation 4024 <= t < 5000; test t >= 5024 (24-step purge).

models.HAR: OLS on [1, x_t, mean of last 10, mean of last 50] (the true linear part has this form).
models.DOM, ISING: dom_lib.features G3 / dom2_lib.ising_features, seeds 0-9, ridge readout (hourly_databento_qrc.ridge_fit) on the HAR residual; prediction = mean over seeds. As dom_run.py / dom2_run.py.
models.ESN28u_t, SAS28_t: dom_lib.esn1 / dom3_lib.sas, 12 configurations each (dom3_lib.ESN_GRID, SAS_GRID), tuning seeds 100, 101 by validation MSE, then seeds 0-9. As dom2_run.py / dom3_run.py.
models.LSTM1: dom3_lib.fit_seq unchanged, one channel (last 10 standardised values), 12 configurations (NN_GRID), tuning seed 100, seeds 0-9. As dom4_run.py.
models.CB: best classical student per dataset = the one of ESN28u_t, SAS28_t, LSTM1 with the lowest VALIDATION MSE.
models.reference_rows_not_students: ORACLE = true conditional mean. DOM_or / ISING_or (QDOM / QISING cells only) = the teacher's own circuit and scaling with a ridge readout: checks that the pipeline can detect a quantum edge when one certainly exists.

statistics: Per dataset: test MSE. Per cell: ratio = exp(mean over the 10 datasets of log MSE ratio); 95% t interval (9 df); two-sided one-sample t test on the log ratios; Holm within each family over all cells. Categories exactly as dom3_report.category with the +/-3% band. Families: Q1 DOM vs CB, Q1 ISING vs CB (primary); Q2 DOM and ISING vs LSTM1 and vs SAS28_t (secondary); R descriptive: CB vs HAR, DOM vs HAR, ISING vs HAR, ORACLE vs HAR, teacher circuit vs CB. Descriptive table: share of the attainable gain captured, (MSE_HAR - MSE_model)/(MSE_HAR - MSE_ORACLE), cells with s >= 0.05.

decision_rules.pipeline_check: PASSED if the teacher's own circuit vs CB is 'meaningful edge' or 'detectable, below band' in at least one QDOM or QISING cell with s >= 0.15. If FAILED, the map is reported as inconclusive (W0) and no headline is drawn.
decision_rules.headline_from_Q1_meaningful_edge: W1: no cell has a meaningful edge -> 'within the conditions tested, the published quantum reservoirs never beat a validation-selected classical model by more than 3%, even on data generated by a quantum reservoir of their own family'. W2: meaningful edges only in QDOM/QISING cells -> 'an edge larger than 3% appears only when the data are generated by a quantum reservoir of the same family and the learnable share is at least s* (smallest such s)'. W3: a meaningful edge in a classically generated cell -> reported as an edge of that reservoir as a feature map for that structure, not as a quantum advantage (the simulation is classical).
decision_rules.secondary_from_Q1_detectable: The same three-way classification applied to 'detectable, below band' cells is reported as a secondary result with that label.
decision_rules.copper_placement: For each copper grid, copper's best single-input network vs HAR (min of LSTM1, GRU1; pooled rolling; dom4_report_rolling.csv) is compared with the synthetic cells' CB vs HAR ratio; cells within +/-0.01 are 'copper-like', and their Q1 categories are reported. The paper may say only 'in synthetic cells where classical models gain as much over HAR as on copper, the quantum reservoirs [category counts]'. It may NOT say copper's structure is known: the map identifies the size of the learnable signal, not its form.

pilot_disclosure: Before registration ONE dataset outside the registered set (long, QDOM, s = 0.15, rep 99) was generated and SCORED to time the code and check the pipeline (output kept in rmap_pilot/). Ratios to HAR: DOM 0.868, ISING 0.872, ESN28u_t 0.881, SAS28_t 0.879, LSTM1 0.876, ORACLE 0.866, teacher circuit 0.865. This was seen before the design was frozen. Changes made after it: share 0.30 added; the captured-gain table added (both because the pilot showed the +/-3% band leaves little room when the classical models already capture most of the gain). The registered reps 0-9 use different noise and teacher seeds.

student_prediction.reading: NOT stated. The student answered 'let's run all'. Left null.

claude_prediction_recorded_for_transpare.text: Pipeline check passes. W1 (no meaningful edge anywhere) because the classical models capture most of the attainable gain. Secondary: DOM 'detectable, below band' on QDOM cells and probably on CSAS cells at s >= 0.15 (same algebraic form), so the secondary result is W3-like; ISING weaker; NULL cells no difference. Copper-like cells (CB/HAR about 0.975-0.985) are at s 0.02-0.05 and show no detectable quantum edge. Informed by the pilot, so not a blind prediction.

known_limits: Synthetic processes chosen by the assistant; the conclusions hold for these structures only. Other structures (regime switching, jumps, heavy tails, several inputs) are not tested.
Single-input reservoirs only (as published); the multivariate claim of Maheshwari et al. is NOT tested here.

The +/-3% band is relative to total MSE including irreducible noise; when the classical models capture most of the attainable gain a 3% edge is impossible. The captured-gain table is reported for that reason.
One pilot dataset was scored before freezing (see pilot_disclosure).
Literature check on whether such a map exists for quantum reservoirs is still to be documented before any novelty claim (script rule 6).
AI-written code not re-derived by the student.
cost_estimate: About 100 s per dataset on one core (pilot: 89 s); 500 datasets on up to 10 cores: about 1.5 to 2 hours. No hardware jobs; no new data purchase.
stop_rule: One run of the 500 registered datasets, report and stop. No further structures, shares, memories, models or categories on this map after results. A crashed job is re-run unchanged.
